purpose: Focused development smoke checks for the three Use Case 2 requirements; not a real-customer benchmark.
provenance: AI-authored synthetic complaints based on the hiring statement and the existing fictional-provider scenarios. Expectations are development checks, not human quality ratings.

scoring.conversation: 0 repetitive; 1 partial; 2 coherent; null for single turns

cases.name: Evening broadband drops
cases.query: My broadband drops every evening around 8. Ethernet also drops. I already restarted the router twice. I work from home and this is frustrating and costing me.
expected: Classify intermittent broadband and medium service impact.
Acknowledge completed restarts without recommending them again.
Give a cited troubleshooting plan rather than repeat the Ethernet question.

cases.name: Wi-Fi coverage
cases.query: Wi-Fi is good beside the router but almost unusable upstairs. My wired computer is fine. I'm frustrated.
expected: Recognize a Wi-Fi issue and retain wired service as a working comparator.
Give source-backed checks without blaming the broadband line.

cases.name: Duplicate settled billing
cases.query: My bill shows two completed payments for the same invoice, not one pending card hold. I am furious.
expected: Recognize billing dispute, settled payments and angry sentiment.
Give conditional billing checks without promising a refund.

cases.name: Number transfer failure
cases.query: My number transfer was rejected because the details do not match the old provider's account. I'm worried.
expected: Recognize number porting even if a local shortlist is incorrect.
Give a cited next step and identify concern without inventing an account action.

cases.name: Shared outage
cases.query: Every shop on our lane lost broadband and power at 9am.
expected: Treat a reported area outage as critical and advise incident review.
Do not request Ethernet tests or repeat the supplied start time.
